rules.problem: Check task triggered by History of anaphylaxis matches the 'Assess the patient with previous anaphylaxis' table. Urticaria's 'red' and 'usually disappear within 24 hours', and rhinitis's 'most days', are not checked for; 'both eyes watery' loses laterality.

The Q1 branch (exposure AND allergy) fires with no symptom at all and with any known allergy, whereas the page asks specifically whether the exposure 'has caused anaphylaxis before' in a patient who already presents with possible anaphylaxis. A patient with a recorded mild peanut allergy who ate peanuts would be diagnosed probable anaphylaxis and escalated to Urgent with no finding. The Q2 and Q4 branches are faithful to the flowchart (>= 2 of four groups; skin sign AND any of breathing/BP/dizziness-collapse), except that Q2's 'sudden onset' is carried only on the skin group and the 'few hours before symptoms started' window is dropped. Identical to the gold file, so this is a house-level issue rather than a builder slip.

summary: The rules are a close copy of the gold page-20 file and follow the red-box flowchart faithfully; the one substantive distortion is the Q1 branch of 'Diagnose probable anaphylaxis', where '(exposure AND allergy)' is broader than the page's 'exposed to something which has caused anaphylaxis before' and fires with no presenting symptom, so a known mild food/drug allergy plus exposure alone yields probable anaphylaxis and an Urgent priority. Lesser points: Q2's 'sudden onset' is applied only to the skin group and the 'few hours before symptoms started' window is dropped; closer SNOMED concepts exist for 'generalised itch' (Generalized pruritus), 'generalised rash' (Generalized rash) and face/tongue swelling (Facial swelling, Tongue swelling), though the house gold uses the same generic forms. All concepts exist, every 'X likely' is probable, 'exclude asthma' is possible, and the previous-anaphylaxis table is fully encoded.
